evidence: 'What is the pattern?' (light and dark on earth, which we call day and night)
rationale: Students engage with the expository text What Makes Day and Night and, during the shared writing portion (Work Time C), identify the main topic when asked "'What is the pattern?' (light and dark on earth, which we call day and night)" and supply supporting information when asked "'What information should we record about this pattern?'" — providing details such as "The earth rotates each day. When the earth faces the sun we have day; when the earth turns away from the sun we have night." These student acts touch the main topic and supporting details clauses, but only partially: the lesson's instructional intent is note-taking and science content recording, not explicitly teaching students to recognize expository craft techniques (main topic and supporting details as text-structure elements). There is no moment where students are asked to identify or name the techniques an author uses to craft an expository text, so the broader "recognize techniques" clause is not met.
standard_raw_text: Identify techniques used to craft expository texts, including main topic and supporting details. (I)
